title: M&A Content Hook Library · August & September 2026
note: A GUIDE, not a calendar (Paul, 2026-08-20: "more of a GUIDE and less of a specific post per day prescription — every month will run a research to see what topics are hot"). Five pillars, each in three hook styles: the Data Drop, the Provocation, the Thesis. A hook is a STARTING POINT, never a post: Paul writes the copy in the app, picks a template, and presses Send to Cowork. One hook may feed three posts or none — nothing here is consumed by being used. Source: Google Doc 10vJNy7CVDKVFCUdhyJtW8o-Z2hy3sadzlmX45ApGUiQ, transcribed verbatim; only the Drive exporter’s escaping and its stray "end list" markers normalised. CHECKED against every market’s retired-figure denylist on 2026-08-20: clean, no known-retired figure. That proves nothing dead is present; it does not prove what IS present is true. Three to verify before they ship: "$1.1 Trillion in dry powder" carries no universe (the Aug 21 calendar’s own Day 23 argues you must name one, and lists $1.2T buyout-only / $2.5T all PE / $3.9T all private capital, with Bain 2026 at $1.3T); the "GF Data 2.8 turn gap" must be the published size-band gradient and not the platform/add-on split, which R-HS-027 retired as subscriber-only; and the "$1.2 Trillion" deal-value figure shares a numeral with the retired sector-segmented dry powder, so never put them on one page.

pillars.title: The Bifurcation
pillars.goal: Highlight the stark contrast between top-tier asset pricing and the rest of the market.

hooks.hook: M&A volume is down 4%, but deal value just hit $1.2 Trillion. The market isn't just bifurcating — it's splitting into two entirely different realities.
hooks.direction: Follow up with the GF Data stat on the 2.8 turn gap, then pivot to how 'The Settlement' bridges this.

hooks.hook: A-tier assets are commanding 2021 peak pricing. Everything else is getting a brutal reality check. Here is why the middle market is feeling the squeeze.
hooks.direction: Discuss the compression of average assets and why buyers are hoarding capital for perfect targets.

hooks.hook: The gap between medium and large deal multiples just hit 2.8 turns. The entire premium now sits on one thing: post-close platform building.
hooks.direction: Lead directly into the P-1 post framework. Explain how platform characteristics dictate who wins the premium.

pillars.title: The Exit Logjam
pillars.goal: Exploit the tension between record capital and record holding periods.

hooks.hook: We have $1.1 Trillion in dry powder waiting to deploy, yet it would take 9 years to clear existing PE inventory. Welcome to the great M&A paradox.
hooks.direction: Break down the friction between buy-pressure and exit constipation.
A punchy one-liner. Follow immediately with the reality of 2020–2022 vintage funds hitting mandatory deployment deadlines and why value creation has to be real now.

hooks.hook: How do you solve buy-side pressure and sell-side constipation at the exact same time? You stop relying on multiple expansion.
hooks.direction: Transition into how functional value creation is the only way to break the logjam.

pillars.title: Risk Migrating into Deal Structure
pillars.goal: Reframe the rise in earnouts not just as a trend, but as the contractualization of market uncertainty.

hooks.hook: An earnout isn't just a deal term. It's the bid-ask gap contractualized.
hooks.direction: The best near-term Provenance post. Explain how the market is converting uncertainty into a deferred reconciliation.

hooks.hook: A third of all small deals are now settling the final price after the close. The risk is migrating directly into the deal structure.
hooks.direction: Use the SRS Acquiom data: 35% of sub-$25M deals have earnouts, compared to the drop in all-cash deals.

hooks.hook: Sub-$25M deals are escrowing 15% of transaction value. Deals over $750M? Just 2.7%. If you are playing in the LMM, the safety net is gone.
hooks.direction: Highlight the disparity in risk tolerance between the LMM and the upper tier.

pillars.title: Diligence as the Kill Floor
pillars.goal: Expose how underwriting rigor has replaced loose capital, and highlight the new diligence dimensions.

hooks.hook: For three consecutive years, inflation was the #1 diligence boogeyman. Today, it's been displaced by geopolitics and tariffs.
hooks.direction: Explore this shift in advisor focus and how it changes the underwriting model.

hooks.hook: QoE discrepancies are doubling. Buyers aren't just being thorough — they are daring your fundamentals to fail.
hooks.direction: Frame diligence as the 'kill floor' where 47% of breaks happen.

hooks.hook: Nearly half of all broken deals die in diligence. If your underwriting rigor isn't flawless, the market will find the model miss.
hooks.direction: Land the P-2 Thursday post here. Focus on the execution hinging on valuation discipline.

pillars.title: AI as Diligence
pillars.goal: Address AI as a constraint/risk rather than hype, and push back on false market narratives (multiples).

hooks.hook: Stop treating AI as a headline. Treat it as a diligence question: will this technology accelerate or erode the target's moat in 36 months?
hooks.direction: Keep to the constraint. Discuss AI purely as a factor of underwriting rigor — did anyone actually diligence the AI risk?

hooks.hook: 13.4x is not your multiple. If your target isn't earning $60M+ in EBITDA, you need to stop looking at headline medians.
hooks.direction: Claim this lane. Deconstruct why sellers anchor to PE mega-deal medians and why LMM advisors have to reset those expectations.

hooks.hook: Acquirers are quietly asking one crucial question in diligence right now: 'Did anyone underwrite the AI risk?'
hooks.direction: Connect the AI moat question directly to the 'Model Misses' concept.
